**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected**: Sugarcane leaf
- **Key visual features**:
  - The leaf displays distinct longitudinal streaking — alternating lighter (pale yellowish-green) and darker green bands running parallel to the leaf veins
  - The streaks extend along the full length of the visible leaf surface
  - No discrete spots, necrotic lesions, or marginal scorch visible
  - The overall leaf texture appears intact; no wilting or distortion
  - The pattern is uniform stripes/streaks rather than irregular mosaic patches

**Reasoning through the classes:**

| Class | Match? |
|---|---|
| **Brown_Spot** | No — no brown spots/lesions present |
| **Grassy_Shoot** | No — single leaf, no shoot proliferation |
| **Leaf_Scald** | Partial — Leaf Scald causes water-soaked streaks but typically shows straw/brown coloration and marginal scorch, not seen here |
| **Pokkah_Boeng** | No — no leaf distortion, twisting, or young shoot malformation |
| **Sett_Rot** | No — affects seed pieces/roots, not leaves |
| **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv** | **Yes** — SCSMV causes fine chlorotic streaks running parallel to veins, creating a streak mosaic of alternating light and dark green bands, exactly matching the image |
| **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus** | Partial — mosaic virus causes irregular light/dark patches, but the pattern here is more linear/streak-like, not irregular mosaic |
| **Yellow_Leaf** | No — Yellow Leaf primarily yellows the midrib; no midrib yellowing visible here |
| **Yellow_Spot** | No — no discrete yellow spots |

The parallel longitudinal streaks of alternating pale-green and normal-green running along the vein axis are the hallmark of **Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus (SCSMV)**.
